stage_a.note: Very strong positive engagement, enthusiastic delivery with big smiles and gestures.
Sustained engagement with the product, showing it off excitedly.
Friendly, approachable, and considerate expression throughout the presentation.

venture.description: A belt buckle that folds down to hold a beverage bottle or can hands-free.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder introduces himself, the product, and asks for the investment, demonstrating how the buckle holds a beverage.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how he came up with the idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he was in college and wanted his hands free to hold his beer while dancing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks to see one of the buckles.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees and hands them out to the investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Notes that it does not come with the belt.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Thanks the founder for handing him the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Comments that the product is heavy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if a magnet holds it closed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that it is held by a magnet.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if there are any sales now.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States he has sold over four thousand units personally at festivals across America.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks over what period of time the sales occurred.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that it was over four years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what that translates to in dollar sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that they are at three hundred and forty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if he has a patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that he does have a patent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what the cost to make the product is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the cost is ten dollars and it sells for thirty-five up to a hundred and ten.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Jokes about asking Kevin since it is a good price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees playfully that it is a pretty good price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what his full-time job is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he just got out of school to be an unexploded ordnance technician.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what that job means.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that it is the identification and remediation of unexploded military ordnance.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Clarifies if it is like looking for bombs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that it absolutely is.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if he wants to do that job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it is a plan B because he needs to provide for his family and a baby on the way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Jokes that the problem with his job is mistakes leave him in five pieces.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that there are no mistakes in that job.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the game plan is for tomorrow if he gets the investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Deflects by offering them to choose between two numbered envelopes.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Chooses envelope number one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the first envelope has a list of retailers who want the product in their stores.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Reads the list of retailers aloud from the envelope.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the second envelope is a list of raceways that want to sell the buckle trackside.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Reads the list of raceways aloud from the envelope.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if any of those companies have written a check.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers no because he has an issue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he had a problem with his manufacturer and his recent order was twenty-six percent defective.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reacts with shock to the defect rate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that it is bad news.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks why he wouldn't take a purchase order from anyone on the list.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he lacks working capital to supply it, but could seal the deal with an advance check.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if he is going to work full time on the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that he absolutely will if he is able to.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what that means and if he needs a salary.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that something has to pay the bills and he would rather not do bombs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks how much money he would need to make it a full-time job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that he needs two to three thousand dollars a month for bills.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Summarizes that nobody wrote a check and he doesn't have time to teach him, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks how much inventory he currently has.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that he has sixty-two units.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: States the math isn't adding up and he's not getting anywhere, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Agrees with Mark that the founder is running fast but standing still and not getting anywhere.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Says he doesn't have a problem with teaching him and will suck up the time.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Offers the fifty thousand dollars for a seventy-five percent stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Encourages him, saying he just needs guidance and is on the right track.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Calls Robert's offer medieval and says it steals people's companies.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Offers fifty thousand dollars for a twelve percent royalty with no equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains he would rather do this deal than see the founder blown up by mines.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that he would also rather be doing the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks the founder how badly he wants this business to succeed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that he wants it really bad and believes the product can boom instead of snail along.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Suggests going to sporting goods stores and opening those avenues up.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Announces that she is jumping in to make an offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Offers fifty thousand for fifty-one percent to knock Robert out of the deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Adds a condition that he cannot take a salary from the investment money.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder it is insane to give up seventy-five percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Criticizes Kevin's offer for sending twelve percent of the cash flow out of the business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Tells him coffee is for closers and urges him to close on one of the offers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reminds him that life is full of choices.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder he has to pick one of the offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts Barbara's offer, stating she is the best person to go into business with.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Compliments him by calling him a smart guy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that it was a good decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Points out that he just gave up control of his company.

decisions.note: Everybody said they wanted it, nobody wrote a check, asking to value at half a million and teach him, won't have time to help.
Math not adding up, same challenges for 4 years, not getting anywhere.
Needs someone to suck up a lot of time and guide him.
Thinks Robert's offer is medieval, would rather do this than see him blown up.
Wants to knock Robert out of the box.

decisions.terms: cannot take a salary from the $50,000
decisions.note: He is overeating and greedy, needs to live on something else.
Thinks she is the best person to come into business with.

record.notes: No major issues. The pitch is straightforward.
